items.ownerBrief:
DECISION NEEDED: what is a member-wanted ad's date, and therefore what does its decide-by derive from?

WHY IT IS OPEN. On 2026-07-30 you ratified 04.01.01 D-16: every post has a decide-by, it is never absent, and no type can publish without one. D-16 splits the twelve types into presence types (decide-by derived from the event date) and delivery types (derived from the stated deadline), and files `Member wanted` with the presence types. Member-wanted ads have no event. 04.06's own Behavior table says the lifecycle is "open-ended; runs for months" and its States table says "no deadline"; the domain CX file's R-02 says the same ("one-to-one, open-ended, unpaid, mutual"); and 04.02.01's board table is the clearest evidence — every other type sorts on a date, member-wanted alone sorts on recency with a 90-day half-life. D-16 therefore derives from an input this type does not carry. This is the platform's highest-volume amateur post.

OPTION A — ask for a real date on the ad. Pro: D-16 holds unchanged; every downstream bound is a date a human stated. Con: it adds a required field to the one post type least able to bear it, and it is a field with no honest meaning — a band seeking a bassist is not deciding by a gig. D-16 was designed precisely to avoid a fifth required interaction ('a default wearing a required field's costume').

OPTION B — derive from a DURATION rather than a date (e.g. published + 90 days). Pro: no new interaction, and the number already exists on the board; 04.02.01 Q-06 has quietly assumed this already, describing the member-wanted decide-by as "a 90-day recency curve". Con: 04.02.01 D-06 states plainly that the board's windows are "presentation only … never a lifecycle transition", so promoting one to a lifecycle input is a decision, not a lookup — and it means an unfilled ad auto-closes on a timer the poster never chose. RECOMMENDED, because it is the only option that keeps D-16 universal at zero interaction cost, and because a downstream file has already assumed it — but the duration must be ratified as a lifecycle value here, not inherited silently from the board.

OPTION C — exempt member-wanted from D-16. Pro: 04.06 and the domain CX stand as written. Con: it reopens every bound D-16 closed — the hold-resolve-by ceiling (04.04.01 D-05), the dormant trigger (04.04.01), and the 'bounded by construction' guarantee that was the whole point of the ratification.

DOWNSTREAM OF YOUR ANSWER: when a member-wanted ad auto-closes; when 04.04.01's `dormant` trigger fires on it; the ceiling on every hold's resolve-by; and 04.02.01 Q-06's abandonment case. Whichever you pick, 04.01.01 D-16's taxonomy row for Member wanted needs sweeping to match — that row is in another agent's shard and is recorded as a cross-domain note.
